You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 

Your task is summarize the modifications made in the patch.
Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

### Modifications Summary

#### Modifications in Each File

1. **`solr/CHANGES.txt`**
   - Added a new entry under "Bug Fixes" for the issue SOLR-9036, which states that the Solr slave was performing full replication of the index after a master restart.

2. **`solr/core/src/java/org/apache/solr/handler/IndexFetcher.java`**
   - Modified the logic to track replication success. The tracking of replication success is now conditional on whether the Solr core is running in ZooKeeper-aware mode (i.e., SolrCloud mode). This change ensures that the last replication success status is only set in the appropriate context.

3. **`solr/core/src/test/org/apache/solr/handler/TestReplicationHandler.java`**
   - Added a new test method `doTestIndexFetchOnMasterRestart` to verify that if the master is down for more than the poll interval, the slave does not re-fetch the entire index if the index has not changed. This test is directly related to the bug fix for SOLR-9036.
   - Introduced a helper method `getSlaveDetails` to retrieve details about the slave's replication status, which is used in the new test.

#### Relationships Between Modifications

- The entry in `CHANGES.txt` documents the bug fix (SOLR-9036) and provides context for the changes made in the codebase.
- The modification in `IndexFetcher.java` is a critical part of the fix, as it alters the behavior of how replication success is tracked, which is essential for preventing unnecessary full replications.
- The new test in `TestReplicationHandler.java` serves to validate the fix implemented in `IndexFetcher.java`, ensuring that the slave behaves correctly after the master restarts and does not perform a full index replication if it is not needed. This test reinforces the changes made and confirms that the bug has been addressed effectively.
